title: BusinessCaseType immutable evidence S6a offline verification

always_on: Issue #687 acceptance criteria and offline-only boundary
scoped: BusinessCaseType S6a DE and EN design specs
on_demand: Revisionssicherheit eventstream policy for future production requirements
runtime: Synthetic in-memory adapters only; no external connector, credential or provider

invariants: AC-S6-01: canonical redacted envelopes accept only declared recoverable phase transitions, contiguous sequence and verified SHA-256 hash chaining
AC-S6-02: factory-verified actor, correlation and event provenance plus an immutable outbox snapshot precede publication under stable bindings
AC-S6-03: ActorRef is tenant-bound and key-versioned, identifiers come from explicit registries, and raw tenant, actor and key material are absent
AC-S6-04: PostgreSQL outbox, broker, separately read anchor, separately read WORM and redacted reconciliation progress are explicit unimplemented production ports
AC-S6-05: retention is at least ten years, stronger provider retention is accepted, legal-hold capability is mandatory and production access review remains unimplemented
AC-S6-06: incomplete or uncertain domain evidence creates a sticky recoverable block; publication failures persist progress but remain intentionally unclosable in S6a
AC-S6-07: output is S6_OFFLINE_FOUNDATION and BLOCKED_PENDING_S7_APPROVAL with every external activity count at zero and no production claim
AC-S6-08: declared provenance, tamper, sequence, binding, completion, redaction, opaque-reference, retention, receipt and separation gates fail closed
required_evidence: Canonical domain and verification contracts with AC-S6-01 through AC-S6-08
Synthetic normal intent-outcome-readback chain and verified chain head
Synthetic reconciliation-required and dual-control closure chain
Deterministic ActorRef vectors proving tenant and key-version binding without raw identity output
Tamper, duplicate, gap, reorder, foreign-binding, incomplete-chain and sensitive-field negative results
Retention, legal-hold, missing-port-receipt and same-principal closure negative results
Synthetic port orchestration with unique broker acknowledgements, bound anchor, WORM receipt/readback and sticky reconciliation on any missing receipt
Redacted CLI smoke output with exact offline and blocked-live statuses and zero external activity
Opaque tenant- and key-version-bound correlation vectors with raw person and matter-like identifiers rejected
Failed mutation plus verified readback terminal-state evidence
Defensive port-copy, event-bound broker ACK, detached anchor bindings, separate WORM readback and substitute-chain rejection evidence
Exact runtime-registry parity for tool, role, BusinessCaseType, catalog version and ETag identifiers
Factory-provenance and post-build mutation rejection at the persisted outbox boundary
Immutable outbox snapshot evidence preventing time-of-check/time-of-use mutation
Unique opaque broker acknowledgements plus exact independent anchor readback
Sticky redacted partial-publication progress and blocked retry evidence
Recovery variants for missing or failed readback and failed closure
Provider WORM retention greater than the event minimum accepted without weakening the minimum
exit_conditions: All eight acceptance IDs are covered by executable checks.
The normal and reconciliation chains pass and every declared negative case fails for the expected stable reason.
The CLI smoke reports S6_OFFLINE_FOUNDATION and BLOCKED_PENDING_S7_APPROVAL without external activity.
No offline artifact claims PostgreSQL durability, detached signature, anchor, WORM retention readback or production reconciliation persistence.
Protected PR checks and independent review are green.
